The dislocation free nature, smooth surface and presence of cracks indicates the brittle fracture behavior of the α–Nb5Si3 phase. Further, from the pile-up of dislocations, it can be inferred that the dislocation movement in the Nbss phase is hindered at the interface of the Nbss and α–Nb5Si3 phases due to the brittle nature of α–Nb5Si3 phase. Consequently, greater amount of stress field generated at the interface and is called plastic constraint. This caused the cracking at the interface of Nbss and α–Nb5Si3 phases
